cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what you feel is as clear to you as the shape of the table.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Choose something you sense about someone close, or about the work you are holding, and stay with it ten minutes. No fixing, no explaining, no next step.
cells.core:
Here the felt sense is steady. What touches you about the people close to you and the work you are holding does not arrive in fragments you must piece together — the whole of it is simply there, and you can carry a room's worth of feeling without it running you. That steadiness is why the structures you build last. A thing built by someone whose feelings are clear does not need propping up later.

What this balance is free to feed is quiet, not more building. Choose something you sense about someone close, or about the work you are holding, and stay with it ten minutes. No fixing, no explaining, no next step. Feeling deepens when it is given room, and you will notice which structures are worth keeping by how they feel to stand inside.
cells.sheetLine: What you feel is clear, and the clarity holds.
cells.verb: knowing what you feel and letting the knowing hold
cells.place: where you build the structure things are held in

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the ending, the summing-up, the moment when this is finished and you can finally relax.
cells.act: decide what this is for before you spend it
cells.ask: Take the next thing you are about to move on, and write one line saying what it is for before you give it anything.
cells.core:
The wholeness is real. Where it tips is the finish line: you are living a few steps ahead of where you are, writing the ending before the middle has happened, and closing in your head what is still open in the day. Structure built at that speed looks like control — deciding who is in, who is out, what this all adds up to — and the people near you can feel the summing-up before it is true.

Seven days, one line. Take the next thing you are about to move on, and write one line saying what it is for before you give it anything. Just the line. The frame goes around the seed, not around the finished thing, and what you already feel stays open long enough to actually arrive.
cells.sheetLine: You are writing the ending before the middle has happened.

cells.tense: You were at a door, it opened, and you are still standing on the same side of it.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: This week, when something stirs — interest, a want, a pull toward a person or a piece of work — catch it before asking what it is for, and follow it ten minutes.
cells.core:
Something finished, and you have not moved into the next stretch. The structures you build have gotten thin — fewer containers, less held — because you are standing where the old ones came apart, still sorting through it instead of starting anywhere new. The wholeness is not gone. It just has nothing to assemble around yet.

Do not push toward feeling. This week, when something stirs — interest, a want, a pull toward a person or a piece of work — catch it before asking what it is for, and follow it ten minutes. That is the whole thing. Sparks do not need a direction to count, and a structure built from one you actually caught will hold better than anything built to prove something is over.
cells.sheetLine: The door opened. You are still on the near side.
cells.verb: knowing what you feel and letting the knowing hold
cells.place: where you build the structure things are held in

cells.tense: You are steering by a compass you do not count as yours, in a place you are already building.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Once this week, where no one is watching and no one will know, do the small fair thing you already sense is owed — and mention it to no one.
cells.core:
The wholeness is operating. You sense what is fair among people before anyone speaks, you feel where the balance has tipped, and you act on it — and if someone named it, your answer would be that anyone would have done the same. The compass reading belongs to you. Your own account of it leaves you out.

Once this week, where no one is watching and no one will know, do the small fair thing you already sense is owed — and mention it to no one. Not because secret is better, but because a thing done without being explained is a thing you can actually own. What drives your structures is a sense of what is right. That sense has an owner, and you are the one already standing there.
cells.sheetLine: The compass reading belongs to you, though your own account drops it.
